newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU delay would mean flood of claims - De Silguy.
newsitem.headline: EMU delay would mean flood of claims - De Silguy.

text.p: European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy has cautioned that a delay in Europe's planned single currency would provoke a flood of compensation claims from banks and big business.

"All the banks and companies who have trusted the (Maastricht) treaty could demand the costs of their preparations back," De Silguy was quoted as saying in an interview with the German news magazine Der Spiegel released on Saturday.
De Silguy said a decision to delay economic and monetary union would constitute a breach of international law, as the Maastricht Treaty lays down a start date of January 1, 1999.
He said this meant the European Union would also face charges of breaking the terms of the treaty in Europe's highest courts if it decided to postpone the project.

Asked what would happen if EU heads of government agreed on a postponement at a meeting next May, he replied: "Then the euro is dead. For a new date after 1999, the treaty would have to be changed, with the whole procedure of ratification in the parliaments of the member states."
The interview was released ahead of publication in Spiegel's next edition, due out on Monday.
